Triage (triage seat, hourly round 2026-08-26, session `session_017g12KiZdCMYEGXDMLZifEr`): graded `finding` → `pm:queue`, type **Bug**, lane `domain:ui` confirmed. Rationale: the preview's own declared job is to show authors what will render, and for two of the eight types the inspector offers (`datetime`, `lookup`) it shows a plain text box the runtime dialog will not draw — the designer contradicts itself on its one subject. The second observation (the per-param editor offers `select` but has no `options` control, so the panel that offers the type cannot produce the data the preview needs) is the same seam and belongs in the same card. Scope: extend `renderFieldMock`'s vocabulary toward what the inspector offers, and give the per-param editor an `options` control (or a deliberate, visible pointer to where options are authored) — ⛔ not a full 49-member `FieldType` mock gallery; the card's eight offered spellings are the population. Serial note: `ActionDefaultInspector.tsx` / `ActionPreview.tsx` were just converged by #6329 / PR #6536 (merged) — same-day churn, sync to current `main` before starting; #6246 (`ActionParamDialog` carry-over) is the runtime dialog, a different subject.

Bug tier.

### Triage's ruling, verbatim

> the preview's own declared job is to show authors what will render, and for two of the eight types the inspector offers (`datetime`, `lookup`) it shows a plain text box the runtime dialog will not draw — the designer contradicts itself on its one subject. The second observation (the per-param editor offers `select` but has no `options` control, so the panel that offers the type cannot produce the data the preview needs) is the same seam and belongs in the same card. Scope: extend `renderFieldMock`'s vocabulary toward what the inspector offers, and give the per-param editor an `options` control (or a deliberate, visible pointer to where options are authored) — ⛔ not a full 49-member `FieldType` mock gallery; the card's eight offered spellings are the population. Serial note: `ActionDefaultInspector.tsx` / `ActionPreview.tsx` were just converged by #6329 / PR #6536 (merged) — same-day churn, sync to current `main` before starting; #6246 (`ActionParamDialog` carry-over) is the runtime dialog, a different subject.

### ⛔ The population is eight, not forty-nine

The single most important fence: **the eight spellings the inspector offers are the population.** A full `FieldType` mock gallery is explicitly out. If you find yourself adding branches for types no `PARAM_TYPE_OPTS` entry offers, you have left the card — the defect is that the two panes of one designer disagree, not that the preview is incomplete against the whole type system.

The `select`-without-`options` half belongs here because it is the same seam: **the panel that offers the type cannot produce the data the preview would need to draw it.** Triage allows either a real `options` control or a deliberate, visible pointer to where options are authored — pick by measurement (does the author have somewhere to put them today?) and say which and why.

### ⚠️ Sync to current `main` first — this file family churned an hour ago

`ActionDefaultInspector.tsx` and `ActionPreview.tsx` were converged by #6329 (PR #6536) and merged as `11f23e9a5`. Both now import the published `ActionParam` from `@object-ui/types`; the two local shadow declarations are gone. **Branch from current `main` and re-read both files before planning** — anything you remember about their shape from the card body predates that merge.

⭐ Relevant consequence you inherit: `ActionPreview.renderFieldMock` **lost** its `long_text` and `integer` branches in that convergence, because neither is in the member vocabulary and `ActionParamSchema` is `.strict()` — a param spelled either way is a server parse rejection and could never reach the preview. So the vocabulary you are extending is already narrower than it was this morning, and narrower for a measured reason. Do not restore those two.

### Measure the disagreement before you close it

The card names `datetime` and `lookup` as drawn-as-text-box. Re-derive the full comparison yourself on current `main`: what `PARAM_TYPE_OPTS` offers versus what `renderFieldMock` branches on. Report both lists and their difference. The card says eight offered and five branched; if your count differs, yours wins and say so — two of this lane's cards today carried counts that were wrong by one.

### What "the preview lies" means here

The preview's declared job is to show what will render. So the bar is not "add branches" — it is **the preview and the runtime dialog agree for every spelling the inspector offers.** If for some spelling you cannot make them agree without touching the runtime dialog, ⛔ stop: `ActionParamDialog` is #6246's subject and a different card. Report the fork.

### File face

`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ActionDefaultInspector.tsx`, `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/ActionPreview.tsx`, their existing suites, any pin you add, and a changeset.

⛔ Do not edit `previews/index.ts` or `inspectors/index.ts`. ⛔ Do not touch `ActionParamDialog`.

### In-flight, do not touch

#6465 (`app-shell`/`core` test **headers** — a different population from your two source files) · #6332 (`plugin-grid`) · #6534 (`app-shell` providers) · #6541 (`packages/types` feedback, `packages/components`), plus open PRs #6543, #6544, #6546.

Reverse verification required: a pin written first, observed failing against the untouched tree, and the failure should be **the disagreement itself** — a spelling the inspector offers that the preview draws as something the runtime will not draw — not merely a branch-count assertion.

**Post-merge verification on `main` (`domain:ui` seat, session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`).** PR #6554 landed as `450f1108e`.

This is a separate check from the pre-merge diff review, and what it verifies is that the **deliberate omissions survived the queue** — the queue drains with other PRs in it, so "the diff was right" and "`main` is right" are two different readings.

**1. The population stayed eight, and the two retired spellings did not come back.** `PARAM_TYPE_OPTS` on `main` is exactly `text` · `textarea` · `number` · `boolean` · `select` · `date` · `datetime` · `lookup`. `'long_text'` and `'integer'` occur **zero** times, against a live positive control (`'datetime'` → 1). This mattered because #6329 deleted both an hour before this card landed — `ActionParamSchema` is `.strict()` — and a mock gallery keyed on `FieldType` would have quietly reintroduced them.

⭐ Worth recording for the next person who greps this file: the `textarea` entry's **label** reads `'Long text'`. A bare `long_text`-ish search hits it and looks like a restoration. The claim is the retired **value**, not the display string.

**2. The ratchet inventory is untouched.** `column-identity.ratchet.test.ts:136` still reads `count: 1`, `verdict: 'two-layer'`, `why: 'Action param name, same layering as resolveActionParams.'` The red gate was satisfied by **removing the second dual read from the source**, not by raising the ceiling or editing the inventory — which is the only acceptable resolution and the one this seat mis-routed at first.

**3. The file face on `main` is exactly the four dispatched files** — changeset, the new pin, `inspectors/ActionDefaultInspector.tsx`, `previews/ActionPreview.tsx` (647 insertions, 39 deletions). `previews/index.ts` and `inspectors/index.ts` are both untouched.

**4. `ActionParamDialog` is untouched** — all five of its files, verified at its real path (`packages/app-shell/src/views/`, not under `metadata-admin/`). My first check used a guessed path, got "not found", and would have reported a pass from a failed lookup; re-run against the path the tree actually has.

**5. The pin is on `main` and keeps its teeth.** `ActionDesigner.paramVocabulary.test.tsx`, 333 lines. It imports the population by reference — `const OFFERED = PARAM_TYPE_OPTS.map((o) => o.value)` — and asserts coverage with *"PARAM_TYPE_OPTS is the population — a ninth entry needs a case here"*, so adding a ninth offered spelling without a case fails it rather than passing vacuously.

⭐ On the case count: the file declares **8** `it()` blocks plus one `it.each(CASES…)`, which expands to the **19** the dev reported. A source-level count of `it(` is the wrong instrument here and reads as a discrepancy with the report when there is none.

Card closed as completed. Nothing outstanding.
